chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about exchanging wheat for barley, and wheat for flour, so he said: 'If they are equal, there is no harm; otherwise, there is not.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for exchanging wheat with barley or flour in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the conditions of *Riba al-Fadl* (excess in exchange) by distinguishing between bulk commodities like wheat and barley versus processed goods like flour. The ruling hinges on whether the items are considered equivalent in measure; if they are equal in quantity, the exchange is valid, but if there is an inequality in the standard measure, it is prohibited. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on precise measurement (*kayl*) in commodity trades to avoid usury.
